purpose: Evaluate embedded LanceDB against agent-maintenance storage requirements before implementation
authorization: Mario requested the local LanceDB test and resumed it after interruption
storage: Private local directory owned by this experiment; synthetic data only

cases.expected: Observation, source harness/session/event and text survive reopen with a null vector
All 60 acknowledged distinct observations remain readable, with exact IDs and provenance
Repeated merge_insert of one capture-operation ID leaves one original
Two simultaneous merge_insert calls of the same capture-operation ID leave exactly one original; rejection is reported separately
Two updates based on revision 0 produce one accepted change and one detectable conflict, with final revision 1
A process can observe another writer's committed observation when configured to refresh; default behavior is recorded separately
SIGKILL after batch-start notification preserves all previously acknowledged rows; interrupted batch is absent or complete, never partial; no claim of exact commit-phase injection
Fixed-vector nearest-neighbor, full-text and hybrid queries honor project filters; null-vector original remains retrievable without embedding generation

followup_if_native_contract_fails: Test a minimal experimental filesystem-lock adapter with fresh reads, operation-key idempotence and revision checks; report its results separately from native LanceDB
limits: Python SDK and local macOS filesystem only; does not establish JS SDK behavior
No models, generated embeddings, cloud services or active agent installation
Fixed vectors validate retrieval plumbing, not semantic quality
Small finite concurrency sample is not a reliability guarantee
Cooperative locks protect only writers using the same adapter
No claim of multi-table transactions or power-loss durability
